stem:
A girl of 4 had a runny nose last week. Since yesterday she has limped, and today she refuses to stand. She was given ibuprofen 2 hours ago, and her temperature is now 38.6°C. She holds the right hip flexed, abducted and externally rotated and resists any passive movement of it. White cells are 13.6 ×10⁹/L, ESR 48 mm/h and CRP 64 mg/L (<5). Ultrasound shows a right hip effusion.

Which diagnosis is most likely?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Transient synovitis often follows a viral illness and also causes an effusion, but the child is usually afebrile or mildly febrile, often bears some weight and has near-normal markers. Fever above 38.5°C despite ibuprofen, refusal to stand, an ESR over 40 and white cells over 12 together make septic arthritis far more likely.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Osteomyelitis also causes fever and raised markers and can coexist with a septic hip, but a hot, immobile hip with an effusion centres her findings on the joint itself.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Perthes disease is an afebrile, gradual limp in a school-age child with normal blood tests.

options.label: D
options.explanation: SUFE affects adolescents around the growth spurt; it causes neither fever nor high inflammatory markers.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Correct. Fever despite ibuprofen, refusal to bear weight, a hip held flexed, abducted and externally rotated, pain on any movement, raised ESR, white cells and CRP, and an effusion mean septic arthritis: an orthopaedic emergency. The preceding cold is the distractor.

options.label: F
options.explanation: JIA needs arthritis for at least 6 weeks. Even systemic JIA, with high fevers and CRP, does not begin as one acutely painful hip overnight.

options.label: G
options.explanation: DDH is a developmental disorder causing a painless limp from early walking. It does not cause fever or an acutely painful hip.

options.label: H
options.explanation: A toddler's fracture causes sudden refusal to walk after a twist, with tibial tenderness, but no fever or raised CRP.

context: A febrile child who will not bear weight, with pain on any hip movement, raised ESR, white cells and CRP and an effusion, has septic arthritis until proved otherwise, even after a viral illness; transient synovitis is a diagnosis of exclusion.
